summary: Bound usage journal admission and preserve fork safety

delivery.outcome: Bound native usage journal admission by its existing 0.5-second SQLite budget; preserve independent-journal progress, fork safety, strict failure and already-produced provider results using the existing inode-scoped SQLite gate.
nonGoals: No provider invocation or paid retry, timeout expansion, resolver edit, credential access, live database mutation or runtime promotion.
Do not claim every cold SQLite failure or worker-start timing issue is resolved.

architecture.decision: Reuse interaction_store._sqlite_write_slot, preserving its default archive budget and fork reset. Allow an explicit private budget for the usage journal so local queueing and SQLite waiting share the existing half-second budget, with inode isolation and normal strict/best-effort failure paths.
architecture.rollback: Revert reviewed source changes; retain fixtures and operational evidence.

commands: Deterministic paused-writer regressions: unrelated journal progress, bounded strict failure and completed provider-result preservation.
validation.evidence: Real record_attempt and complete calls cannot wait indefinitely behind an unrelated or busy writer; no paid request is retried.

commands: Real fork child write while the parent writer is paused, native SQLite default-budget regressions, affected coverage, scripts/verify, current-base OneDev and independent App merge.
validation.evidence: Child and parent can both persist their own metadata; archive admission retains its existing five-second default and data/privacy invariants.
